questions: Did the changes in your face begin suddenly, within the past 24 hours?
Do you have weakness or drooping on either side of your face?
Do you have weakness or numbness in an arm or leg?
Have you had trouble speaking, swallowing, walking, or understanding others?
Have you had a sudden severe headache, dizziness, or loss of consciousness?
Do you have new vision loss or double vision?
Do you have severe facial pain, eye pain, or a severe headache?
Do you have a fever or a new rash, blisters, or swelling on your face?
Have you recently had an injury or procedure involving your face?
Have you recently received Botox, filler, or another cosmetic injection?
Have you used a new skin-care product, cosmetic, medication, or hair product recently?
Is the facial appearance causing itching, burning, or tenderness?
Have you ever had a similar episode before?
Do you have a history of stroke, Bell’s palsy, migraine, autoimmune disease, or skin disease?

results: 1. Complete facial skin examination in neutral expression and during facial movements
2. Full cranial nerve and neurologic examination
cranial nerve examination: involuntary blepharospasm with perioral and jaw dystonic spasms, provoked by speech and eating; otherwise normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
3. Palpation of the forehead, periorbital skin, and facial muscles
4. Dermoscopic examination of any abnormal pigmented or textured skin lesions
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Primary (idiopathic) Meige syndrome — segmental cranial dystonia causing blepharospasm with perioral and oromandibular dystonia

ALTERNATIVE: Tardive cranial/oromandibular dystonia due to dopamine-blocking medication exposure

ALTERNATIVE: Hemifacial spasm

ALTERNATIVE: Wilson disease–associated dystonia
